title: European White Elm: Old White Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: The floodplain elm that mostly shrugged off Dutch elm disease. Berlin's Great Elm of Treptower Park has its roots in the Spree.
intro: This is the elm that likes wet feet. Ulmus laevis is a floodplain tree, and Berlin's Great Elm of Treptower Park takes that literally: its roots run straight into the Spree, which foresters credit for a vigour unusual at 250 years. It was added to Germany's national heritage list on 25 September 2025. The damp ground it favours is also why it mostly escaped Dutch elm disease, which took nearly every other big elm in Europe. Gdansk's stands by the pond in Park Oliwski, 4.2 metres round and 30 metres tall, protected together with the ivy that flowers up its trunk in October. The Dutch register calls the Elm of Heure, on an estate near Borculo, the thickest elm in the Netherlands and records no girth to back it. Munich's register says no older elms are known anywhere in the city than its twin trees in the Englischer Garten.
